ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Sustainability
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Nature Sustainability will publish significant original research from a broad range of natural, social and engineering fields about sustainability, its policy dimensions and possible solutions. Understanding how to ensure the well-being of current and future generations within the limits of the natural world is the overarching goal of sustainability research. Nature Sustainability will cover topics including water, air and soil pollution, agriculture and food security, water–energy–land nexus, water-soil-waste nexus and climate change, among many others.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Boosting water evaporation with clever surface design
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01843-6

Efficient evaporation is crucial for solar-powered water purification, resource recovery and energy utilization, yet boosting evaporation without using more energy remains challenging. Here, a smart surface on which water binds weakly, thereby enabling rapid solar evaporation, makes clean, sustainable water production more efficient.
ns1:item.dc:title: Boosting water evaporation with clever surface design
ns1:item.dc:creator: Shuai Guo
Zhen Yu
Swee Ching Tan

ns1:item.ns1:title: Accelerating water desorption at heterostructure interfaces for high-rate solar evaporation
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 15 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01934-4

Solar interfacial evaporation is a promising solution for water purification. Here this work addresses the bottleneck of slow kinetics of water molecule desorption by constructing a dual-phase heterostructure that achieves a superior evaporation rate with excellent durability.
ns1:item.dc:title: Accelerating water desorption at heterostructure interfaces for high-rate solar evaporation

ns1:item.ns1:title: Minimizing climate change adaptation trade-offs in African rangelands
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Sustainability, Published online: 14 September 2026; doi:10.1038/s41893-026-01938-0

Changing rainfall patterns and intensity make adaptation a necessity for African pastoralists. Paired weather forecasting and risk smoothing help manage the trade-offs inherent to these adaptations.
